answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 124 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is recorded against the sable challenge, the harbor audit can replay the cedar history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 94 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
